title: Period-104 highway conjecture for Langton's ant
formal: Does every finite initial set of black cells in the standard two-color Langton ant process eventually produce a period-104 diagonal highway? Precisely, do there always exist an integer \(T\ge0\) and \(v\in\{(-2,-2),(-2,2),(2,-2),(2,2)\}\) such that for every \(t\ge T\), the ant's position and direction satisfy \(p_{t+104}=p_t+v\) and \(d_{t+104}=d_t\)?
definitions: Cells are the integer lattice \(\mathbb Z^2\), initially white except for an arbitrary finite set. One ant starts at an arbitrary cell facing north, east, south or west. At a white cell it turns right by 90 degrees; at a black cell it turns left by 90 degrees. It then flips that cell's color and moves one unit forward. The position p_t and direction d_t refer to the state before step t. There is no finite boundary or wrap-around. The conclusion concerns the future walk and headings, not translation of the entire colored grid, which retains the trail.
answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof or refutation of the stated proposition, with all its quantifiers and hypotheses. Verification of finitely many parameter values does not establish the universal assertion.
why: A concrete prediction problem for a tiny computational dynamical system: does every finite perturbation eventually organize into a repeating drifting walk?

context_blocks.text: The standard two-color rule is crucial. The 2025 paper disproves analogous highway expectations for other, multicolor turn rules while retaining the original conjecture.
